detail: Look at the rectangle drawn below. Draw a point at the center of the rectangle. Now draw a line segment from the top-left corner to the point you drew. Draw another line segment from the bottom-right corner to the same point. What geometric objects did you draw? Select all that apply.
Look at the two rays below that share a common endpoint. What geometric figure do these two rays form together?
Look at these four shapes: a square, a rectangle, a triangle, and a trapezoid. Which shapes have both parallel sides AND perpendicular lines?

Look at the shape below. It has 4 sides. Two sides are parallel to each other, and the other two sides are also parallel to each other. Does this shape have any right angles? Choose yes or no, then explain which type of quadrilateral it is based on its parallel sides.

Ms. Chen is designing a garden layout. She draws four different quadrilaterals on graph paper and measures their properties:

- Figure A: Has 2 pairs of parallel sides, 4 right angles, and all 4 sides are equal length
- Figure B: Has 2 pairs of parallel sides, 4 right angles, but only opposite sides are equal length
- Figure C: Has 1 pair of parallel sides and no right angles
- Figure D: Has no parallel sides and only 1 right angle

Which figures can be classified as rectangles?

A shape has 4 sides with opposite sides that are parallel to each other. Two of its angles are right angles, and two are not. Which statement correctly describes this shape?

A) It is a rectangle because all angles are right angles.
B) It is a parallelogram because opposite sides are parallel, but NOT a rectangle because not all angles are right angles.
C) It is a rectangle and a parallelogram.
D) It is none of these shapes.
A carpenter is building four different picture frames. Frame A is a square, Frame B is a rectangle, Frame C is a rhombus, and Frame D is a trapezoid. Which frames always have exactly 4 right angles?

Which of these figures has at least one line of symmetry that you could fold along to make matching parts?

Maria has a pizza cut into 4 equal slices. She eats 1 slice. Which fraction shows an equivalent amount of pizza if the same pizza were cut into 8 equal slices instead? Draw or explain how the number and size of parts change, but the amount of pizza stays the same.

Draw or describe how you know Maria and Jake ate the same amount of chocolate. Explain why 1/4 is equivalent to 2/8 using the number and size of the parts.

Draw or describe a visual model showing why 2/3 is equivalent to 4/6. Explain how the number of parts and the size of each part are different, even though the fractions are the same size.

Maria has a chocolate bar divided into 10 equal pieces. She eats 6 pieces. Her friend has a chocolate bar of the same size divided into 5 equal pieces.
